description: See all your Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code chats next to the terminal: which agents are working, which need you, and how full each context is. Compact with a cheaper model, get a reminder before the cache expires, and resume after a usage limit. Reads only the local session logs; the extension makes no network requests unless you allow network access (off by default); today only optional push notifications use it. Unofficial; not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Google or Alibaba Cloud. Free for personal and noncommercial use; commercial use needs a license.
capabilities.untrusted: In Restricted Mode, the settings that point to other folders or programs (Claude Code CLI path, Claude projects folder, Codex, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code folders) are only read from your user settings. Push notification settings and network access are always read only from your user settings.

config.title: Agent Monitor
config.scope: Which sessions the Sessions list, the Overview, the status bar light and the badges include.
config.scope.workspace: Only sessions whose folder is in the current workspace.
config.followActiveChat: When you switch to a Claude Code or Codex chat tab, select that session in the Sessions list. This only happens when you switch tabs, never on a data refresh.
config.hideCompleted: Hide finished subagents, workflow agents and completed workflows in the Agents table and the Overview. The main agent is always shown.
config.showStatusBar: Show the overall status light in the status bar.
config.statusBarBackground: Give the status bar item a warning background when something needs you, and an error background when something failed.
config.showCost: Show API-equivalent costs (estimated from token counts at list API prices).
config.sessionListPosition: Which side of the Agent Monitor panel shows the session list. `auto` puts it on the same side as the terminal's tab list (`#terminal.integrated.tabs.location#`).
config.sessionListPosition.auto: Same side as the terminal's tab list (right by default).
config.sessionListPosition.left: On the left, with the agents on the right.
config.sessionListPosition.right: On the right, with the agents on the left.
config.notifyNeedsYou: Notify you when a chat or agent starts waiting for your reply or approval: a message in the focused VS Code window (except for the chat you are looking at), or a system notification when no VS Code window has focus (macOS and Linux). On Windows and in remote windows, the message appears in the next VS Code window you switch to instead. Each wait is reported by one window only.
config.refreshSeconds: How often to re-read the session logs, in seconds.
config.activeWindowMinutes: Show sessions that were active within this many minutes. Open sessions and the selected session are always shown.
config.staleMinutes: Mark an agent as having no activity after this many minutes without new log lines.
config.approvalGuess: When an open session can't report its real state, guess that an agent is waiting for your approval if a tool call has had no result for a while. Claude Code versions that report their live state are never guessed.
config.approvalGuess.fastTools: Only for quick tools (reading, writing and editing files, search, patches). Long commands such as shell commands are never guessed.
config.approvalGuess.allTools: For every tool, after the no-activity time (staleMinutes).
config.approvalGuessSeconds: In quick-tools mode, how many seconds a quick tool call can go without a result before it counts as possibly waiting for approval.
config.backgroundRefreshSeconds: How often, in seconds, to re-read the session logs while no VS Code window has focus. It applies only when it is longer than `#agentMonitor.refreshSeconds#`. Lower values make "needs you" notifications arrive sooner.
config.shareScanAcrossWindows: Let all VS Code windows share one reading of the session logs: one window reads them and the others show its results, which saves CPU and memory. Turn off to have each window read them on its own.
config.claude.projectsDir: Folder with the Claude Code session logs. Leave empty to use `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects` or `~/.claude/projects`.
config.claude.cliPath: Path to the Claude Code command-line program, used only when you compact a closed session in the background. Leave empty to look for `claude` on your PATH, then in the installed Claude Code extension.
config.codex.home: Codex home folder. Leave empty to use `$CODEX_HOME` or `~/.codex`.
config.copilot.enabled: Read the GitHub Copilot Chat session logs that VS Code keeps (chat and agent mode).
config.gemini.home: Gemini CLI folder. Leave empty to use `$GEMINI_CLI_HOME/.gemini` or `~/.gemini`.
config.qwen.home: Qwen Code folder. Leave empty to use `$QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR`, `$QWEN_HOME` or `~/.qwen`.
config.compactConfirm: Ask for confirmation before compacting a closed session in the background.
config.compactTemplate: Text pre-filled after `/compact` when you compact a session (what the summary must keep). Leave empty to use the built-in template in your display language.
config.contextHintStart: For models with a window of 500K tokens or more: from this many context tokens on, suggest compacting or starting a new session at the next good stopping point.
config.contextHintAct: For models with a window of 500K tokens or more: from this many context tokens on, recommend dealing with the context before auto-compact kicks in mid-task.
config.cacheReminder: Remind you shortly before a large idle session's prompt cache expires, while compacting it is still cheap. Only for the 1-hour cache.
config.cacheReminderMinutes: How many minutes before the prompt cache expires to remind you.
config.cacheReminderMinContext: Only remind about sessions with at least this many context tokens.
config.cacheReminderShortTtl: Also remind about sessions that use the 5-minute cache.
config.closeReminder: When you close a large Claude Code session while its cache is still warm, offer to compact it or write a handoff note.
config.postCompactHint: After a session is compacted, remind you to check that its key rules and constraints are still there.
config.network.allow: Allow Agent Monitor to make network requests. **Off by default**: while it is off, the extension makes no network requests at all. Today only push notifications (`#agentMonitor.push.enabled#`) and their test messages use it; nothing else does. Read only from your user settings, so a workspace can't turn it on.
config.push.enabled: Send a short push message to your phone or team chat when an agent needs you, stops with an error, or reaches or leaves a usage limit. Off by default; choose where it goes with [Push Notifications…](command:agentMonitor.push.setup). Only the project folder name and the state are sent (chat titles and subagent names only with `#agentMonitor.push.includeTitle#`). It uses the network, so it also needs `#agentMonitor.network.allow#`; while that is off, push is paused.
config.push.events: Which events send a push while push is on.
config.push.events.needsYou: An agent is waiting for your reply or approval (pushed only if it still waits after the delay).
config.push.events.error: An agent stopped with an API error.
config.push.events.limitHit: A usage limit of Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI or Qwen Code is reached.
config.push.events.usageHigh: A usage window reaches the usage alert percentage.
config.push.events.costDaily: Today's estimated cost passes your daily budget (the amount isn't sent).
config.push.events.contextHigh: A chat's context reaches the alert percentage of its auto-compact point.
config.push.delaySeconds: How many seconds an agent must keep waiting for you before it is pushed. The desktop notification comes first; if you answer within this time, nothing is pushed. `0` pushes right away.
config.push.includeTitle: Also send the chat title (and the subagent's name). Only a real title is sent (one you set, or one the agent or app wrote); a title made from your first prompt never is.
config.push.channels: Where pushes go (only the parts that are not secret). Add, test, edit or remove channels with [Push Notifications…](command:agentMonitor.push.setup) rather than editing this list: tokens, keys and webhook URLs are kept in VS Code's secure storage, not here.
config.alerts.usagePercent: Alert when a usage window reaches this percentage: Codex's 5-hour and weekly limits (Claude Code doesn't record a percentage). Shown like a "needs you" notification, once per window. `0` turns it off.
config.alerts.dailyCost: Alert once a day when today's estimated API-equivalent cost (Claude Code and Codex together) passes this many US dollars. `0` (the default) turns it off.
config.alerts.contextPercent: Alert when a chat's context reaches this percentage of its auto-compact point, once until it compacts again. `0` (the default) turns it off.
config.sound.enabled: Play a sound when an agent needs you, stops with an error or finishes, and with threshold alerts (`#agentMonitor.alerts.usagePercent#`). Off by default. Each event plays in one VS Code window only, and never in a remote window. Quiet hours mute sounds (`#agentMonitor.quietHours.enabled#`).
config.sound.needsYou: Sound when an agent starts waiting for your reply or approval (it plays with the `#agentMonitor.notifyNeedsYou#` notification). `default` is Glass; `off` plays nothing. The names are macOS sounds; Linux and Windows play a similar system sound.
config.sound.error: Sound when an agent stops with an error or hits a usage limit. `default` is Basso; `off` plays nothing.
config.sound.done: Sound when an agent finishes and you haven't looked at the result yet. `default` is Hero; `off` plays nothing.
config.sound.alert: Sound for threshold alerts (usage, today's cost, context). `default` is Funk; `off` plays nothing.
config.quietHours.enabled: Quiet hours: from `#agentMonitor.quietHours.start#` to `#agentMonitor.quietHours.end#` there are no sounds, no system notifications and no push (`#agentMonitor.push.enabled#`). Messages in VS Code, the panel and the badges still update; a notification waits for the VS Code window you switch to next. The status bar tooltip says when quiet hours are on.
config.quietHours.start: When quiet hours start, as `HH:MM` (24-hour clock, your local time).
config.quietHours.end: When quiet hours end, as `HH:MM`. An end before the start runs past midnight (22:00–08:00).
config.quietHours.days: The days quiet hours start on (`sun` … `sat`). Empty means every day.
config.quietHours.allowErrors: During quiet hours, still let errors through: when an agent stops with an API error or hits a usage limit, the error sound plays and the push is sent. Everything else stays quiet.
config.onlyWorkspace: Only show sessions from the current workspace.
config.onlyWorkspace.deprecated: Replaced by the scope setting (agentMonitor.scope). An existing value is migrated automatically.
